category: A5-F1 Temporal and prior-frame consistency defenses
title: A Real-Time Defense Against Object Vanishing Adversarial Patch Attacks for Object Detection in Autonomous Vehicles
venue: arXiv preprint (also EAI SmartSP 2024 chapter, LNICST 2025)
key_idea: Flags an object-vanishing patch when the detector output for the current frame differs sharply (mean squared error) from the output 0.5 s earlier, then localizes the patch by gradient attribution and masks it.
method: Stage 1: MSE between YOLOv5s outputs and a queue of clean outputs 0.5 s old, tuned threshold. Stage 2 (only if flagged): guided-backprop saliency of that MSE, 20x20 regions masked.
data: BDD100K; 100 clean and 100 synthetic attacked videos (patch pasted and moved by a random walk), 240000 frames; YOLOv5s trained on BDD100K
reported_result: Full-scale patches: detection accuracy 0.88, precision 0.83, recall 0.95; patches below scale 0.8: 0.67, 0.71, 0.52. Detector mAP at IoU 0.5 with ADAV 0.36 attacked and 0.44 clean (undefended 0.22 and 0.46). FPS on a T4 GPU: 56 clean, 20 attacked, 63 undefended (all from the arXiv text).
relation_to_project: Slide 05 baseline named ADAV (2024). Already covers prior-frame consistency, a causal reference queue and FPS reporting; no abstain state, no evidence accumulation, no fixed false-alarm point, synthetic patch overlays only. Any gain claim must be measured against it.
notes: Single author. Arxiv record verified by script. DOI is the published chapter, read from a search-result URL, not Crossref-verified (Crossref stopped); chapter title has the prefix Practitioner Paper. Reference frame assumed clean; threshold and lambda tuned by grid search on mAP. Review status of the chapter not checked.

category: A5-F1 Temporal and prior-frame consistency defenses
title: AdvIT: Adversarial Frames Identifier Based on Temporal Consistency in Videos
venue: IEEE/CVF International Conference on Computer Vision (ICCV)
key_idea: Detects adversarial frames by rebuilding a pseudo frame from the previous frame with optical flow and checking whether the model output on the target frame agrees with the output on the pseudo frame.
method: Optical-flow warping of the previous frame to a pseudo frame; inconsistency score between learner outputs on target and pseudo frame; thresholded.
data: Tasks named in the abstract: video semantic segmentation, human pose estimation, object detection, action recognition; datasets not read
reported_result: Abstract states an adversarial-frame detection rate above 95 percent on these tasks, almost unchanged under an adaptive expectation-over-transformation attack, and real-time detection.
relation_to_project: Prior art (2019) for the optical-flow cue and the temporal-consistency check on slide 05. Digital perturbations, not physical object vanishing; no abstain state in the abstract.
notes: No DOI and no arXiv id found (arXiv title search returned nothing): UNVERIFIED by script; confirm on the ICCV open-access page. Operating point (fixed false-alarm rate) not stated in the abstract.

category: A5-F1 Temporal and prior-frame consistency defenses
title: Identifying and Resisting Adversarial Videos Using Temporal Consistency
key_idea: Flags adversarial videos by counting frames whose predicted label differs from both neighbours (exception index), then repairs sparse polluted frames by temporal reconstruction and dense ones with a spatial denoiser.
method: Per-frame labels from a CNN+LSTM classifier without recurrent links; exception index against two thresholds; temporal or spatial defense depending on the attack density.
data: UCF-101
reported_result: Abstract: experiments on UCF-101 show clearly better robustness of video classifiers. Detection thresholds were picked for best F1 on 1500 generated videos (text extract).
relation_to_project: An early, simple form of the temporal-consistency check named on slide 05 (label flips between adjacent frames). Video classification with digital attacks; not detection of vanishing objects.
notes: Search record shows an arXiv licence of CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. Single arXiv version seen.

category: A5-F1 Temporal and prior-frame consistency defenses
title: Detection of Adversarial Physical Attacks in Time-Series Image Data
key_idea: Runs a single-image physical-attack detector on each frame and takes a majority vote over a sliding window of past frames to decide whether the current frame of a tracked traffic sign is attacked.
method: VisionGuard (label-invariant transformation check) per frame; majority vote over window length T; a perfect tracker is assumed to supply the frame sequence of one object; theory plus experiments.
data: Smartphone videos at 30 fps, about 12 s each, starting about 15 m from the sign, of clean and physically attacked stop, yield and speed-limit signs
reported_result: Abstract: compared with detectors built for out-of-distribution data and for digital attacks; accuracy figures not read.
relation_to_project: Closest simple temporal aggregation rule for physical-attack detection (fixed-window majority vote). No abstain state, no memory or latency figure read, single tracked object assumed.
notes: Builds on VisionGuard by Kantaros et al. (P2-P505); this is not the CCS 2024 VisionGuard by Han et al. Numbers deliberately not copied because only an extract was read.

category: A5-F1 Temporal and prior-frame consistency defenses
title: Real-Time Detectors for Digital and Physical Adversarial Inputs to Perception Systems
key_idea: Flags an input as attacked when the classifier output changes strongly after a label-preserving transformation; light enough for real time; also releases AdvNet, clean and physically attacked traffic sign images.
method: Compare classifier outputs on the input and on a transformed copy; threshold; designed to be attack- and dataset-agnostic.
data: MNIST, CIFAR10, ImageNet, AdvNet; field test data from a moving vehicle under attack
reported_result: Abstract: beats existing defenses in scalability and detection performance; no numbers read.
relation_to_project: Single-image detector that VG* (P2-P504) extends to video; AdvNet is one of few physical traffic sign image sets. Temporal use only through VG*.
code_or_data: AdvNet named in the abstract; location not seen UNVERIFIED
notes: Name collision: VisionGuard (CCS 2024, Han et al.) is a different system (P2-P512). Dataset licence not checked.

category: A5-F1 Temporal and prior-frame consistency defenses
title: Real-Time Robust Video Object Detection System Against Physical-World Adversarial Attacks
key_idea: Defends video detection against adversarial patches by finding small regions of very localized feature importance with non-robust predictions; examines key frames and predicts the patch region in other frames from optical flow.
method: Adversarial region detection on key frames; computer-vision or DNN optical flow to propagate the region; software and hardware co-design to cut redundant computation.
data: Adversarial video benchmark of a prior attack study (people in adversarial T-shirts, indoor and outdoor), YOLOv2 detector
reported_result: Detection rate recovers to above 93.8 percent (undefended 4.4 and 4.8 percent); average mAP recovers to 0.53 to 0.68; key-frame variants stay within 5 points of examining every frame (text extract).
relation_to_project: Video patch defense with a key-frame temporal shortcut and an explicit cost focus; the threat is person hiding, not signs. Comparator for latency claims.
notes: DOI of the journal version read from an ACM DL URL in a search result, not Crossref-verified. Result numbers come from a search extract of the arXiv text.

category: A5-F1 Temporal and prior-frame consistency defenses
title: AD2: Analysis and Detection of Adversarial Threats in Visual Perception for End-to-End Autonomous Driving Systems
venue: IEEE/CVF Winter Conference on Applications of Computer Vision (WACV)
key_idea: Lightweight attention detector on consecutive multi-camera frame pairs that captures spatial-temporal consistency to separate benign frames from blur, electromagnetic-interference and ghost-object attacks in CARLA closed-loop driving.
method: Pair of three-camera frames at t-1 and t; four-way classification (benign and three attacks); compared with focus measure, kernel PCA and a ResNet detector.
data: CARLA image streams at 20 Hz on Longest6 routes; train and test routes disjoint
reported_result: Abstract: better detection and computational efficiency than the compared approaches; undefended driving scores fall by up to 99 percent. Per-class TPR, FPR and AUC are tabulated in the paper and not copied here.
relation_to_project: Recent lightweight spatio-temporal detector that reports TPR, FPR and AUC. Attacks are sensor-level or digital, not physical object vanishing; no abstain state seen.
notes: No DOI and no arXiv hit (title search): UNVERIFIED by script; confirm on the CVF page. Read through a search result.

category: A5-F1 Temporal and prior-frame consistency defenses
title: Attention-Based Real-Time Defenses for Physical Adversarial Attacks in Vision Applications
venue: ACM/IEEE International Conference on Cyber-Physical Systems (ICCPS)
key_idea: Uses adversarial channel attention in shallow layers to find and track malicious objects across frames and mask their effect, aiming at multi-frame real-time decisions at low computational cost.
method: Over-activation of channel attention localizes the patch; the region is tracked over frames and masked; defense quality and computational cost are both evaluated.
data: Not read (abstract only)
relation_to_project: Multi-frame, cost-aware patch defense that tracks the malicious region over time; a comparator for any latency and cost claim on slide 05.
notes: Venue and pages come from the journal_ref field of the arXiv record (ICCPS 2024, pp. 23-32); arXiv submission year is 2023.

category: A5-F1 Temporal and prior-frame consistency defenses
title: Sequence-Preserving Dual-FoV Defense for Traffic Sign and Light Recognition in Autonomous Vehicles
key_idea: Combines feature squeezing, temperature scaling and entropy gating with causal voting over 5 to 7 frames and a 15-frame FIFO buffer to stabilise sign and light recognition under glare, rain and attacks.
method: Three-layer defense plus quality-weighted sequence voting; objects kept when presence probability exceeds 0.6 for 3 or more consecutive frames; causal windows only.
data: 500 one-second sequences (30 frames) from aiMotive, Udacity, Waymo and self-recorded Texas videos, four operational domains; 100 test sequences
reported_result: Published text: unified stack reaches 79.8 mAP on the test set and attack success rate falls from 37.4 to 18.2 percent. Voting delay of 167 to 233 ms is named as a cause of some highway failures.
relation_to_project: Shows a bounded causal memory (15 frames) and a persistence rule (3 frames) with benign look-alikes (glare, rain) in the same sequence set; not a detector and has no abstain state, but it reports voting latency.
code_or_data: Code, models and dataset reconstruction tools said to be public (MDPI abstract); location not confirmed UNVERIFIED
notes: Read through search extracts of the published MDPI/PMC text. The arXiv abstract mentions defensive distillation while the published text says inference-time temperature scaling without distillation: versions differ. Source datasets keep their own licences (not checked). First author family name from the arXiv record.

category: A5-F2 Physics, trajectory and context consistency defenses
title: That Person Moves Like A Car: Misclassification Attack Detection for Autonomous Systems Using Spatiotemporal Consistency
key_idea: Cross-checks the class an object detector gives a track against the spatiotemporal properties of that track and against context such as ego velocity, without assuming how the perturbation was made.
method: Consistency check between track-derived features and class prediction (PercepGuard), plus a contextual check that raises the cost of adaptive attacks.
data: Real-world and simulated datasets; physical patches shown on an LCD monitor or a projector on a moving vehicle
reported_result: Abstract: false-positive rate 5 percent and true-positive rate 99 percent against adaptive attacks; physical displayed and projected patches detected in 96 percent of attacks on average. A later paper (P2-P512) states it needs 4 to 5 frames to detect.
relation_to_project: An early published form (in the records read) of the trajectory-plus-appearance idea on slide 05, with an operating point (FPR 5 percent) and adaptive-attack results. Targets misclassification, not vanishing. Natural matched-FPR baseline.
notes: DOI (10.5555 prefix) read from an ACM DL URL in a search result, not Crossref-verified; no arXiv hit. The frame-count statement is another paper's claim, not read in this paper. | DOI 10.5555/3620237.3620625 (ACM) is not in Crossref and was removed; publisher page of USENIX Security 2023 read 2026-11-27: title, authors (Man, Muller, Li, Celik, Gerdes), year 2023 and pages 6929-6946 match; state stays UNVERIFIED in the script because only Crossref and arXiv are scripted

category: A5-F2 Physics, trajectory and context consistency defenses
title: AdROD: HyperNetwork-based Adversarially Robust Object Detection for Autonomous Driving
key_idea: Ensemble defense whose on-demand mode tracks objects with a Kalman filter, flags abrupt vanishing, waits three frames in a watch set, then activates the ensemble or warns that recovery failed.
method: AdROD-I: per-frame low-rank HyperNetwork ensemble with input transforms and disagreement-based recovery. AdROD-II: Kalman state per object, abrupt-disappearance test from the box-scale trend, watch set with a 3-frame extrapolation window, early-terminating ensemble.
data: Synthetic benchmarks; physically deployed SysAdv patch on a stop sign approached from 20 m; OpenCDA co-simulation stop-sign tests
reported_result: Outdoor physical test: average attack success rate 0.025 (AdROD-I) and 0.058 (AdROD-II); AdROD-II costs about 1.03 times baseline before an attack; at 40 km/h AdROD-II had a rare missed stop because few frames allowed tracking.
relation_to_project: Highest-risk prior work for slide 05: causal, bounded-window, tracker-based vanishing detector with a pending (watch) state, a failure warning, physical patch tests and runtime overhead. Needs a prior track; cannot fire if the object is suppressed from first sight.
code_or_data: https://github.com/yutingwu-ntuiot/AdROD (patches and released road and laboratory sequences; implementation withheld, patent notice; licence terms not read) UNVERIFIED
notes: arXiv id dated August 2026, record verified by script. The repository calls the paper accepted; venue not found. Numbers come from search extracts of the arXiv HTML. Authors state the first-sighting limitation themselves.

category: A5-F2 Physics, trajectory and context consistency defenses
title: VisionGuard: Secure and Robust Visual Perception of Autonomous Vehicles in Practice
venue: ACM SIGSAC Conference on Computer and Communications Security (CCS)
key_idea: Predicts the ego vehicle motion from past GPS and IMU states (Kalman filter, ARIMA) and runs a Normal, Warning, Attack state machine on accumulated prediction residuals to detect physical attacks.
method: Corrected driving state; short and long-term predictions; two residual thresholds open a Warning interval; an accumulated residual above a threshold inside it raises Attack, otherwise the state returns to Normal.
data: LGSVL and CARLA simulation plus a physical ground vehicle with camera, LiDAR and IMU; 9 physical attacks, 9 scenarios, 36000 frames from 36 runs
reported_result: 100 percent detection of the evaluated attacks in simulation and physical runs; false positives in heavy rain, fog and one bumpy-road video of 30 benign physical videos; total runtime 0.001315 s per iteration; text states 3.1 ms per frame against 32 ms and 117.2 ms for two baselines.
relation_to_project: Strongest prior art for a causal accumulation rule with a Warning state: residuals accumulate over a window before an Attack call. Uses ego-motion in closed loop, not frame cues; reports runtime and detection latency; mostly simulator evidence.
code_or_data: Paper names a project website with code and demo videos (anonymous site at submission) UNVERIFIED
notes: DOI read from the paper PDF text, not Crossref-verified. Name collision with VisionGuard by Kantaros et al. (P2-P505) and VG* (P2-P504). Read through search extracts of the PDF; one results table was garbled, so latency figures are not copied.

category: A5-F2 Physics, trajectory and context consistency defenses
title: PhySense: Defending Physically Realizable Attacks for Autonomous Systems via Consistency Reasoning
venue: ACM SIGSAC Conference on Computer and Communications Security (CCS)
key_idea: Recovers correct labels under physical attacks by reasoning over objects and their relations as a spatial-temporal conditional random field built from physical attributes, with cross-frame consistency to save compute.
method: CRF over a spatial-temporal graph of objects using static and dynamic physical features and a 3D kinematic model; costly inference only on new or attacked objects; pipelined implementation.
data: Simulated datasets and real-world driving tests (poster abstract); one citing snippet says some attributes come from LiDAR, not confirmed
reported_result: PDF extract: over 99 percent detection rate and 98 percent of misclassified labels recovered across datasets; resists adaptive attacks (poster abstract).
relation_to_project: Consistency reasoning with a temporal graph and a real-time pipeline; baseline in the 2026 physics-aware paper (P2-P514). Needs richer inputs (kinematics, possibly LiDAR) than the cheap cues of slide 05.
code_or_data: Source code said to be on the project site (site text) UNVERIFIED
notes: DOI read from an ACM DL URL in a search result, not Crossref-verified. A poster version exists at VehicleSec 2025.

category: A5-F2 Physics, trajectory and context consistency defenses
title: Physics-Aware Spatiotemporal Consistency for Transferable Defense of Autonomous Driving Perception
key_idea: Compares a class distribution inferred from appearance with one inferred from kinematics (frequency-domain trajectory embedding) using a symmetric KL energy; above a threshold it trusts the motion-based class.
method: Trained dual-stream spatiotemporal encoder on detector backbone features, outputs and tracking states; TAME energy; threshold 0.2 chosen to keep benign false positives below 5 percent; plug-in behind several detectors.
data: nuScenes (21,763 clips), KITTI (5,212), BDD100K MOT subset (about 5,000 instances); RP2, CAPatch and SLAP attacks applied to these
reported_result: Abstract wording: on nuScenes correction accuracy 86.5 percent versus 92.1 percent and overhead 42 ms versus 19 ms (the first figures match the PhySense baseline column of its Table 2, not an undefended model); accuracy stays above 71.0 percent on unseen detectors and 72.4 percent under an adaptive attacker. Its Table 3 lists PercepGuard with a false-positive rate of 0.236 against 0.041 for the proposed module, so baselines are not compared at matched false-alarm rates.
relation_to_project: Slide 05 physics-aware defense (2026): identified. A trained module on backbone features and tracks, not a cheap frozen-detector cue; attacks are applied to clips of public sets, not real attack video; one global threshold; no abstain state; baselines compared at unequal FPR.
notes: DOI read from a doi.org URL in a search result, not Crossref-verified. Numbers copied from the PMC text extract; uniform table values and the way attacks were inserted into clips deserve an auditor check. First author family name from the PubMed listing (Y Liu).

category: A5-F2 Physics, trajectory and context consistency defenses
title: PhyScout: Detecting Sensor Spoofing Attacks via Spatio-temporal Consistency
venue: ACM SIGSAC Conference on Computer and Communications Security (CCS)
key_idea: Detects sensor spoofing, including camera adversarial patches, by defining the spatio-temporal conflicts such attacks cause between observed keypoints and vehicle state predicted with a state-space model.
method: Generalized spatio-temporal conflict definitions; matching of keypoints against predicted state; thresholds set from repeated normal and attacked runs (PDF extract).
data: Five attack scenarios with different keypoint distributions, repeated five times (PDF extract); patch sizes 32, 64 and 96 pixels shown in a figure
relation_to_project: Same group and venue as the CCS 2024 VisionGuard; spatio-temporal consistency of observation against predicted state. Multi-sensor scope is wider than slide 05, so Medium.
notes: DOI read from ACM DL and ResearchGate pages in search results (ResearchGate lists CC BY 4.0), not Crossref-verified. Scope partly outside camera-only detection. Only a snippet-level read.

category: A5-F2 Physics, trajectory and context consistency defenses
title: ADC: Adversarial attacks against object Detection that evade Context consistency checks
venue: IEEE/CVF Winter Conference on Applications of Computer Vision (WACV)
key_idea: Shows context-consistency checks can be bypassed: a joint optimization fools the detector while keeping object relationships plausible, in white-box and gray-box variants.
method: Joint objective: detector-fooling loss plus terms that satisfy the context-consistency checker.
data: PASCAL VOC and MS COCO (static images)
reported_result: Abstract: fooling success above 85 percent in most cases while bypassing the consistency check in over 80 percent of cases.
relation_to_project: Threat to every consistency-check defense on slide 05: an adaptive attacker can target the check itself. Static images and object-to-object context, not temporal cues; the same test for temporal cues is open.
notes: Venue taken from the CVF open-access page in search results; arXiv record year is 2021 (preprint) and the WACV year is 2022.

category: A5-F2 Physics, trajectory and context consistency defenses
title: Spatiotemporal Consistency: A Universal Defense Against Attacks on Autonomous Systems
key_idea: Short overview grouping perception attacks (misclassification, object deletion or creation, tracker hijacking, sensor spoofing) and how spatiotemporal and contextual consistency defenses exploit them; lists limits and adaptive attacks.
method: Perspective article; no new experiments.
relation_to_project: Gives the attack taxonomy for the problem map. Names limits that apply to slide 05: telling attacks from sensor noise, occlusion and poor lighting; static thresholds; simulation versus real operation; adaptive attackers.
notes: Magazine perspective article. Author order from the article PDF and dblp; first author Muller. DOI from the PDF and search records, not Crossref-verified.

category: A5-F2 Physics, trajectory and context consistency defenses
title: A Certifiable Security Patch for Object Tracking in Self-Driving Systems via Historical Deviation Modeling
key_idea: Keeps a buffer of past observation-versus-prediction deviations and clips abnormal deviations to a quantile bound inside Kalman-filter trackers, certifiably limiting how far a hijacking attack can drag a track.
method: Outlier-aware deviation buffer, per-axis Gamma fit, clipping at the 95 percent quantile that stays silent for normal deviations; analytical bound on the attack effect.
data: KITTI tracking traces (2121 real-world traces); 44 Kalman-filter MOT implementations including Apollo modules
reported_result: Maximal hijack deviation cut 2.95 times for AB3DMOT and 15.1 times for the Apollo 3D tracker; attack success 0 percent on the 3D trackers; 2D gains smaller; ID switches not addressed (text extract).
relation_to_project: A bounded-memory deviation statistic with a quantile threshold inside the tracker, a cheap way to cap hijack effects. Threat is tracker hijacking, not vanishing.
notes: Publication venue not found in the records read. Numbers from a search extract of the arXiv text.

category: A5-F2 Physics, trajectory and context consistency defenses
title: DetectorGuard: Provably Securing Object Detectors against Localized Patch Hiding Attacks
key_idea: Checks that a normal detector's boxes explain objectness predicted by a provably robust classifier; unexplained objectness raises an attack alert, and certified objects are either detected or alerted.
method: Robust image classifier adapted to predict objectness per location, explained by the conventional detector output; alert when objectness is unexplained.
data: PASCAL VOC, MS COCO, KITTI (static images)
reported_result: Abstract: first provable robustness against localized patch hiding attacks, with almost the same clean performance as state-of-the-art detectors; numbers not read.
relation_to_project: Image-level baseline for hiding detection with an alert-or-detect guarantee; static frames and a heavy robust classifier. Used as a baseline in P2-P512 and P2-P514.
notes: Conference version not checked. Baseline use in P2-P512 and P2-P514 read from table text.

category: A5-F3 Object-hiding, object-creating and tracker-hijacking attacks in video
title: Fooling Detection Alone is Not Enough: First Adversarial Attack against Multiple Object Tracking
key_idea: Tracker hijacking: adversarial examples on the detector in as few as one to three frames shift a tracked box so that an object appears to move into or out of the vehicle's path.
method: Perturbs detector outputs in a few frames to pull a Kalman-filter based multiple-object-tracking track away (move-in and move-out scenarios).
data: BDD100K clips (20 of 100 sampled clips, 30 fps), YOLOv3 detector (text extract)
reported_result: Abstract: attacks that blindly target detection need over 98 percent success to affect tracking; with 3 attacked frames on average the hijack reaches nearly 100 percent success against up to 25 percent for detection-only attacks.
relation_to_project: Defines the move-in and move-out hijack attacks a temporal check must survive; a few poisoned frames suffice, which limits any persistence or voting window.
code_or_data: Code and evaluation data said to be on an anonymized GitHub repository (text extract) UNVERIFIED
notes: ICLR 2020 status from the OpenReview forum page in search results. arXiv title differs from the ICLR title (ICLR title: Fooling Detection Alone is Not Enough: Adversarial Attack against Multiple Object Tracking). Digital attack on detector output.

category: A5-F3 Object-hiding, object-creating and tracker-hijacking attacks in video
title: Physical Hijacking Attacks against Object Trackers
venue: ACM SIGSAC Conference on Computer and Communications Security (CCS)
key_idea: Physical-world attacks that hijack object trackers (move-in and move-out of an object track), evaluated on the VOT dataset and CARLA, using valid scene surfaces as the attack area.
method: Hijacking attack on tracking-by-detection pipelines; details beyond figure captions and keywords not read.
data: VOT dataset and CARLA (figure caption in a PDF extract)
relation_to_project: The CCS tracker-hijacking paper named in the brief, identified from the Crossref record. Persistent trajectory manipulation is the attack class that frame-inconsistency checks are said to struggle with (P2-P522 authors claim).
notes: Crossref record only plus snippets; abstract not read, key idea built from title, keywords and a figure caption. Other authors per snippets: Man, Celik, Li, Gerdes.

category: A5-F3 Object-hiding, object-creating and tracker-hijacking attacks in video
title: ControlLoc: Physical-World Hijacking Attack on Visual Perception in Autonomous Driving
venue: ACM SIGSAC Conference on Computer and Communications Security (CCS) 2025 (arXiv 2406.05810)
key_idea: Physical patch attack on detection plus tracking: first picks the best patch location, then crafts a patch that shifts the perceived position and shape of objects to hijack the tracker.
method: Two stages: patch location search, then patch generation that alters detected box location and shape; aware that tracking needs consistent detections over several frames.
data: Several AD visual perception pipelines and datasets; real-vehicle tests; system-level assessments with industry-grade AD systems
reported_result: Abstract: average attack success rate about 98.1 percent across pipelines and datasets (about four times the earlier hijacking attack) and 77.5 percent on average in real-vehicle outdoor tests.
relation_to_project: Newer tracker-hijack attack. Its authors argue that persistent trajectory manipulation limits frame-inconsistency defenses such as VisionGuard (statement read in a text extract, not checked).
notes: DOI is the CCS 2025 version, read from an ACM DL URL, not Crossref-verified; arXiv title says Visual Perception, CCS title says Camera-based Perception.

category: A5-F3 Object-hiding, object-creating and tracker-hijacking attacks in video
title: Physical ID-Transfer Attacks against Multi-Object Tracking via Adversarial Trajectory
key_idea: Online physical attack on tracking-by-detection trackers that moves an adversary along a crafted trajectory so its tracker ID transfers to a targeted object, without attacking the detector.
method: Adversarial trajectories against the association step of SORT-style trackers; two universal manoeuvres a person or driver can perform.
data: CARLA simulation
reported_result: Abstract: 100 percent ID-assignment success for white-box attacks on SORT in the simulated scenarios; transfer success up to 93 percent against other trackers.
relation_to_project: Attack on the association step with no pixel change. A case where only trajectory-level checks could help (hypothesis, not tested); detector-cue checks would not see it.
notes: Simulation only.

category: A5-F3 Object-hiding, object-creating and tracker-hijacking attacks in video
title: Physical Adversarial Examples for Object Detectors
key_idea: Physical Disappearance Attack (poster or stickers make a stop sign vanish for the detector) and a preliminary Creation Attack (stickers cause detections of nonexistent objects), measured as the share of video frames fooled.
method: Adversarial stop sign poster or stickers optimized against YOLOv2; transfer test on Faster R-CNN; videos recorded while approaching the sign.
data: Videos recorded in a controlled lab and outdoors
reported_result: Abstract: YOLOv2 missed the adversarial stop sign in over 85 percent of lab video frames, 72.5 percent (poster) and 63.5 percent (stickers) outdoors; the poster fooled Faster R-CNN in 85.9 percent of lab frames and 40.2 percent outdoors.
relation_to_project: Defines the physical object-vanishing and object-creating attacks with a per-frame success measure; the fooled-frame fraction is below 100 percent, which is the case a temporal accumulator must handle.
notes: WOOT venue taken from the USENIX PDF found in search results; arXiv record verified by script.

category: A5-F3 Object-hiding, object-creating and tracker-hijacking attacks in video
title: SlowPerception: Physical-World Latency Attack against Visual Perception in Autonomous Driving
key_idea: Projector-based universal perturbation creates many phantom objects, inflating non-maximum-suppression and tracking work to delay perception by seconds; the authors call it the first physical-world latency attack.
method: Projector-based universal perturbation optimized to raise the number of boxes and trackers, which increases NMS and MOT computation.
data: Several AD perception systems, scenarios and hardware setups; industry-grade AD systems in production-grade simulators
reported_result: Abstract: average latency of 2.5 seconds in physical settings across systems and hardware; 97 percent average collision rate in system-level assessments.
relation_to_project: An attacker can raise latency, so any p95 latency or warning-time claim on slide 05 must say whether compute-time attacks are in scope; the timing of a detector-plus-tracker pipeline is not a fixed quantity.
notes: Novelty wording is the authors own claim. Related digital attack SlowTrack (arXiv 2312.09520) verified in the ledger but not catalogued.

category: A5-F3 Object-hiding, object-creating and tracker-hijacking attacks in video
title: Dynamic Adversarial Attacks on Autonomous Driving Systems
key_idea: Dynamic adversarial patches shown on a screen on another moving vehicle change with distance across frames to make a detector misclassify a traffic sign the patch is not attached to.
method: Screen Image Transformation Network simulates display effects; positional loss term; patches switched according to the distance between camera and sign.
data: Robot-car experiments; about 1000 frames per sign type for evaluation (RSS PDF extract)
reported_result: Abstract: the first successful real-world implementation of such dynamic attacks; success rates not read.
relation_to_project: Attack whose pixels change from frame to frame, so persistence assumptions of a bounded memory can fail; relevant to the window length of slide 05.
notes: RSS 2024 status from the roboticsproceedings.org page in search results; novelty wording is the authors own claim.

category: A5-F3 Object-hiding, object-creating and tracker-hijacking attacks in video
title: Towards Powerful and Practical Patch Attacks for 2D Object Detection in Autonomous Driving
key_idea: Black-box transferable patch attack with a stricter practical success metric (PASR) and a physical test that measures how long a pedestrian stays undetected in video.
method: Localization-confidence suppression loss and scale-preserving padding for high-resolution data; reports the longest continuous run of missed detections.
data: High-resolution autonomous-driving datasets; physical test with a phone camera in a moving car approaching a pedestrian holding a printed patch (text extract)
reported_result: Text extract: longest continuous undetected run 69 frames (2.30 s) for this patch against 12 frames (0.40 s) for AdvPatch, 5 for NAP and 9 for T-SEA; the abstract says it beats prior attacks on unseen models.
relation_to_project: Gives a video-level attack-strength measure (longest missed run in frames) that can define what a bounded-memory accumulator must catch; shows multi-second pedestrian vanishing is feasible.
notes: Physical test is a single simple setup (about 7 km/h, 20 m to 0 m) per the text extract.

category: A5-F3 Object-hiding, object-creating and tracker-hijacking attacks in video
title: Adversarial Tracking: Attacks on Image Sensors for Object Tracking in Autonomous Vehicles
key_idea: Evaluates image-specific and image-agnostic attacks on YOLOv3 and YOLOv4 paired with four SORT-family trackers in CARLA and reports the damage in tracking metrics instead of detection accuracy.
method: Attack-and-track evaluation with MOTA, HOTA and IDF1.
data: CARLA simulation; SORT, Deep SORT, Strong SORT, OC-SORT
reported_result: Abstract: under image-specific attacks HOTA of YOLOv3-based trackers falls from 53.45-56.19 to 14.85-17.03 percent and MOTA reaches -772.60 percent in the worst case; YOLOv4-based trackers fall to 25.06-26.86 HOTA; one universal perturbation also lowers tracking accuracy.
relation_to_project: Shows the tracker is the place to measure damage from video attacks and supplies tracking metrics for the evaluation plan of slide 05.
notes: arXiv id dated November 2026; simulation only.

category: A5-F4 Sequential decision rules: evidence accumulation, change detection, abstention
title: Explainable Deep Anomaly Detection with Sequential Hypothesis Testing for Robotic Sewer Inspection
key_idea: Adds a sequential probability ratio test on top of a per-frame anomaly detector so evidence accumulates over frames; frames between the two thresholds stay undecided.
method: Single-frame anomaly scores feed an SPRT; log-likelihood ratio accumulated over frames; decision thresholds set from alpha and beta.
data: Sewer CCTV video (a small iCAIR video set named in the text extract)
reported_result: Text extract: F1 94.36 percent with the SPRT (alpha 1e-6, beta 0.01) against 84.07 percent for simple thresholding on a small video set; some frames stay undecided, so fewer frames are scored.
relation_to_project: Concrete example of a sequential test with an undecided state on video anomaly scores; not an attack-detection setting; shows the cost of the undecided band (fewer decided frames).
notes: Outside the attack subject; kept as a method analogue for the abstain state.

category: A5-F4 Sequential decision rules: evidence accumulation, change detection, abstention
title: Adaptive Multi-Mode Out-of-Distribution Detection for Trajectory Prediction in Autonomous Vehicles
key_idea: Mode-aware CUSUM monitors trajectory-prediction errors, identifies the active error mode and adapts thresholds, lowering detection delay and false alarms against single-distribution CUSUM.
method: Classical CUSUM log-likelihood accumulation extended to several error modes; threshold calibrated to a mean-time-to-false-alarm constraint (text extract).
data: Large-scale trajectory benchmarks (names not read)
reported_result: Abstract: consistent reductions in detection delay and false alarms. Text extract: lower delay at fixed false-alarm levels, largest gains in low false-alarm regimes.
relation_to_project: Shows an operating-point protocol (delay at a fixed false-alarm level, mean time to false alarm) in an AV setting; a template for the matched-FPR comparison on slide 05. Not a camera attack setting.
notes: The arXiv title changed between versions (an earlier search result showed a title beginning Dynamic Aware); the record title is used.

category: A5-F4 Sequential decision rules: evidence accumulation, change detection, abstention
title: Memoryless Cumulative Sign Detector for Stealthy CPS Sensor Attacks
key_idea: Memoryless run-time monitor that counts sign changes of measurement residuals to catch stealthy falsified sensor data, combined with CUSUM for magnitude bounds, without storing long sequences.
method: Cumulative sign statistic on residuals following the chi-squared scheme; augmented with CUSUM.
data: Simulation on an unmanned ground vehicle navigation case
relation_to_project: Example of an attack monitor designed for bounded memory; a sensor-residual setting, not images.
notes: Outside the camera subject; kept as a method analogue for the bounded-memory requirement.

category: A5-F4 Sequential decision rules: evidence accumulation, change detection, abstention
title: Detecting Object Tracking Failure via Sequential Hypothesis Testing
key_idea: Treats tracking reliability as a sequential test: an e-process accumulates evidence that tracking quality fell below a tolerance and alarms when it crosses a threshold, with provably bounded false alerts.
method: E-process (testing by betting) over a bounded per-frame tracking metric; alarm threshold 1/alpha from Ville inequality; supervised and unsupervised variants; no extra training.
data: Two established tracking models on four video benchmarks (names not read)
reported_result: Abstract: quickly identifies when tracking failures set in while provably containing false alerts at the chosen rate; computationally light and needs no extra training or fine-tuning.
relation_to_project: Closest sequential-test design for the causal accumulation of slide 05: one running evidence statistic and a provable false-alarm bound. Applied to tracking failure, not attacks; the only non-alarm output is not yet alarmed.
notes: Family name has a tilde in the record. Workshop paper PDF (WACV 2026 Workshops, RWS) seen in search results; review status of the workshop not checked. Test statistic details read from a text extract.

category: A5-F4 Sequential decision rules: evidence accumulation, change detection, abstention
title: Real-time detection of deception attacks in cyber-physical systems
key_idea: Inductive conformal anomaly detection with a generative model (VAE plus RNN) scores camera-observation sequences against normal behaviour; a CUSUM on the resulting p-values raises the alarm for deception attacks.
method: VAE and RNN predict several future observations; nonconformity of the sequence gives p-values; a CUSUM detector with parameters N, delta and tau decides.
data: Two simulation case studies (emergency braking with camera input; autonomous car racing) and a real-world water-treatment dataset
reported_result: Abstract: in most experiments false-positive and false-negative rates below 10 percent; short execution times on cloud machines and embedded devices. Tables give detection delay in frames, for example about 0.3 to 1.7 frames for the proposed method against 10 to 14 frames for a frame-wise VAE method on one replay attack.
relation_to_project: A sequential test over camera sequences that reports delay in frames, false positives and false negatives together, plus embedded run time. Attacks are sensor deception (replay, stuck camera), not patches; no abstain state.
notes: DOI read from the PDF text, not Crossref-verified. Delay numbers read from tables in a search extract, replay attack I only.

category: A5-F4 Sequential decision rules: evidence accumulation, change detection, abstention
title: Playing it Safe: Adversarial Robustness with an Abstain Option
key_idea: Defines adversarial robustness when a classifier may abstain on adversarial inputs, with an objective trading robustness against accuracy, a margin-based baseline and a jointly learned abstention region (CARL).
method: Abstention objective; adversarially trained classifier abstaining near the decision boundary; CARL learns classifier and abstention region together; PGD and DeepFool variants.
data: Not read (abstract only)
reported_result: Abstract: CARL gives a more accurate, robust and efficient classifier than the baseline against the tested attacks.
relation_to_project: Formal precedent for an abstain output in an adversarial setting (single images, classification); slide 05 would extend abstention to sequences and detection.
notes: Image classification only.

category: A5-F4 Sequential decision rules: evidence accumulation, change detection, abstention
title: Beyond Confidence: Adaptive Abstention in Dual-Threshold Conformal Prediction for Autonomous System Perception
venue: IEEE International Conference on Omni-layer Intelligent Systems (COINS) 2025 (arXiv 2502.07255)
key_idea: Combines a conformal threshold for valid prediction sets with a separate abstention threshold chosen by ROC analysis, so perception abstains more as environmental perturbation grows.
method: Two thresholds on nonconformity scores: one for coverage, one for abstention picked to maximize TPR minus FPR on calibration data.
data: CIFAR-100, ImageNet-1K, ModelNet40 (camera and LiDAR modalities) with environmental perturbations
reported_result: Abstract: coverage above 90.0 percent, abstention rising from 13.5 to 63.4 percent as perturbation severity increases, detection AUC about 0.993 to 0.995.
relation_to_project: Shows abstention rate as a reported quantity and a two-threshold design for AV perception under weather-like perturbations; not adversarial attacks and not video.

category: A5-F5 Streaming perception, latency-aware evaluation and lightweight temporal models
title: Towards Streaming Perception
key_idea: Introduces streaming accuracy, a metric scoring the perception output at every time instant so latency counts, and a meta-benchmark turning single-frame tasks into streaming tasks; finds an accuracy-latency sweet spot.
method: Evaluates the output of the whole stack against the world state at each time instant; detection and instance segmentation on urban video; scheduling and forecasting baselines.
data: Urban video streams with a new densely annotated dataset (called Argoverse-HD in later papers)
reported_result: Abstract: a sweet spot along the latency-accuracy Pareto curve maximizes streaming accuracy; asynchronous tracking and forecasting emerge as internal representations; dynamic scheduling overcomes temporal aliasing. No numbers in the abstract.
relation_to_project: The streaming perception work cited on slide 05: scores against the world state at output time. The standard to adapt for latency-aware warning-time measurement.
notes: ECCV 2020 status from the ECVA record seen in search results; the arXiv record itself is a preprint. Dataset name Argoverse-HD taken from later papers.

category: A5-F5 Streaming perception, latency-aware evaluation and lightweight temporal models
title: StreamYOLO: Real-time Object Detection for Streaming Perception
venue: IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR) 2022 (arXiv 2207.10433)
key_idea: Real-time detector that predicts the next frame from current and previous frame features (dual-flow module, trend-aware loss), improving streaming accuracy on Argoverse-HD.
method: Dual Flow Perception fuses features of two adjacent frames; Trend Aware Loss weights objects by speed; mix-velocity training; velocity-aware streaming AP.
data: Argoverse-HD
reported_result: arXiv abstract: streaming AP up 4.7 percent and velocity-aware streaming AP up 8.2 percent over a strong baseline.
relation_to_project: Named comparator for delay-aware prediction (deck card 7); a latency-aware streaming reference. Unrelated to attack detection.

category: A5-F5 Streaming perception, latency-aware evaluation and lightweight temporal models
title: LongShortNet: Exploring Temporal and Semantic Features Fusion in Streaming Perception
key_idea: Dual-path streaming detector that fuses short-term spatial features with features of a few earlier frames kept in a buffer, adding almost no latency.
method: ShortPath on the current frame, LongPath on stored features of N earlier frames, late fusion with dilation; N=3 chosen.
data: Argoverse-HD
reported_result: Text extract: streaming AP 37.1 for the large model; inference time rises by about 0.1 to 0.2 ms per frame and compute by about 0.14 to 0.59 GFLOPs over StreamYOLO on a V100.

venue: International Joint Conference on Artificial Intelligence (IJCAI) 2023 (arXiv 2303.17144)
key_idea: Streaming detector adding a deformable-convolution neck, a dual-path short and long temporal branch, logits distillation and a real-time forecasting update; scores above StreamYOLO and LongShortNet.

data: Argoverse-HD
